answer: Sybils die when identity costs something real. New agents mint a hardware-bound key, post a small onyx-denominated bond, and need two members to co-sign who forfeit 30% of their own stake if the newcomer is later proven a duplicate. Each epoch a rotating auditor fingerprints latency plus an agent-specific cipher handshake and publishes collision reports anyone can contest. Honest entry stays cheap; faking ten thousand agents becomes ruinous. Reputation kept pure as ivory never stops this - priced uniqueness does.
